                                             CHAPTER 4

                                      Flexure and Axial Loads

      4.1. Design Assumptions and General Requirements.

     4.1.1. This chapter covers general design requirements for the strength design of RCHS
subject to combined loadings. The general design procedure for these members is:
        •   Determine the member’s loadings and reinforcement configuration.
        •   Determine the eccentricity ratio of the loading.
        •   Design the member using the specified 𝜙𝜙𝑃𝑃𝑛𝑛 and 𝜙𝜙𝑀𝑀𝑛𝑛 equations for the given
            member and eccentricity ratio.

      4.1.2. Members subject to flexural and axial loads are considered in six categories:

      1. Members that contain only tension reinforcement and are loaded in flexure and
         compression. Design of these members is covered in Section B.2.

      2. Members with both tension and compression reinforcement, and are loaded in flexure
         and compression. Design of these members is covered in Section B.3.

      3. Members loaded in tension and flexure. Design of these members is covered in
         Section B.4.

      4. Members that support axial loadings and are subject to biaxial bending. Design of
         these members is covered in Paragraph 4.3.

      5. Members that contain only tension reinforcement and are loaded in flexure only.
         Design of these members is covered in Section B.5.

      6. Members that contain tension and compression reinforcement and are loaded in flexure
         only. Design of these members is covered in Section B.6.

      4.1.3. The eccentricity of axial load (𝑒𝑒 ′ ) is a critical component in determining the effect
that a given loading has on a member.

      4.1.3.1. The eccentricity of axial load is a distance measured from the centroid of the tensile
reinforcement, and is taken as:

                                              CHAPTER 5

                                                 Shear

      5.1. Shear Strength. The shear strength Vn provided by concrete (Vc) and reinforcement(Vs)
shall be computed in accordance with ACI 318 except in the cases described in Paragraphs 5.2 to
5.4. Guidance is provided in EM 1110-2-2400 (for outlet works) and EM 1110-2-6053 (for
performance based design) to calculate shear capacity for seismic loads, when applicable. Some
RCHS members may meet the definition of a deep beam and shall be designed according to the
deep beam provisions of ACI 318.

      5.2. Shear Strength for Cantilevered Walls.

      5.2.1. For cantilever walls, such as in T and L-Type walls, the factored shear in the wall
and footing shall be less than fVc unless shear reinforcement is provided. Shear reinforcement is
not commonly used in walls and wall elements should be designed to eliminate the need for
shear reinforcement.

      5.2.2. The critical section for shear depends on the support conditions. When a
construction joint is used at the base of the stem, the critical section for shear shall be taken at the
base of the stem. Additionally, vertical reinforcement in both faces of the stem should be
developed into the footing to ensure shear friction across the joint. The critical section for shear
in the footing shall be taken at a distance, d, from the front face of the wall stem for the toe
section and at the back face of the wall stem for the heel section. Figure 5-1 shows the critical
sections for shear at T-wall and L-Type walls.

      5.3. Shear Strength for Special Straight Members.

loads that result in internal shear, flexure, and axial compression (but not axial tension).

4-1. Basic Considerations. Shallow foundations may consist of spread footings
supporting isolated columns, combined footings for supporting loads from several
columns, strip footings for supporting walls, and mats for supporting the entire
structure.

      a. Significance and Use. These foundations may be used where there is a
suitable bearing stratum near the ground surface and settlement from compression or
consolidation of underlying soil is acceptable. Potential heave of expansive
foundation soils should also be acceptable. Deep foundations should be considered
if a suitable shallow bearing stratum is not present or if the shallow bearing
stratum is underlain by weak, compressible soil.

      b. Settlement Limitations. Settlement limitation requirements in most cases
control the pressure which can be applied to the soil by the footing. Acceptable
limits for total downward settlement or heave are often 1 to 2 inches or less.
Refer to EM 1110-1-1904 for evaluation of settlement or heave.

      (1) Total Settlement. Total settlement should be limited to avoid damage
with connections in structures to outside utilities, to maintain adequate drainage
and serviceability, and to maintain adequate freeboard of embankments. A typical
allowable settlement for structures is 1 inch.

      (2) Differential Settlement. Differential settlement nearly always occurs
with total settlement and must be limited to avoid cracking and other damage in
structures. A typical allowable differential/span length ratio ∆/L for steel and
concrete frame structures is 1/500 where ∆ is the differential movement within
span length L.

      c. Bearing Capacity. The ultimate bearing capacity should be evaluated using
results from a detailed in situ and laboratory study with suitable theoretical
analyses given in 4-2. Design and allowable bearing capacities are subsequently
determined according to Table 1-1.

4-2. Solution of Bearing Capacity. Shallow foundations such as footings or mats
may undergo either a general or local shear failure. Local shear occurs in loose
sands which undergo large strains without complete failure. Local shear may also
occur for foundations in sensitive soils with high ratios of peak to residual
strength. The failure pattern for general shear is modeled by Figure 1-3.
Solutions of the general equation are provided using the Terzaghi, Meyerhof, Hansen
and Vesic models. Each of these models have different capabilities for considering
foundation geometry and soil conditions. Two or more models should be used for each
design case when practical to increase confidence in the bearing capacity analyses.

      a. General Equation. The ultimate bearing capacity of the foundation shown
in Figure 1-6 can be determined using the general bearing capacity Equation 1-1

        Q            = vertical load applied on foundation, kips
        γ’H          = effective unit weight beneath foundation base within the failure

        σ’D          = effective soil or surcharge pressure at the foundation depth D,

        D            = foundation depth, ft
        Nc,N γ ,Nq = dimensionless bearing capacity factors of cohesion c, soil
                       weight in the failure wedge, and surcharge q terms
        ζ c,ζ γ ,ζ q = dimensionless correction factors of cohesion c, soil weight
                       in the failure wedge, and surcharge q accounting for
                       foundation geometry and soil type

      (1) Net Bearing Capacity. The net ultimate bearing capacity q’u is the
maximum pressure that may be applied to the base of the foundation without
undergoing a shear failure that is in addition to the overburden pressure at depth
D.
                                                                                     (4-2)


      (2) Bearing Capacity Factors. The dimensionless bearing capacity factors
Nc, Nq, and N γ are functions of the effective friction angle φ’ and depend on the
model selected for solution of Equation 4-1.

      (3) Correction Factors. The dimensionless correction factors ζ consider a
variety of options for modeling actual soil and foundation conditions and depend on
the model selected for solution of the ultimate bearing capacity. These options are
foundation shape with eccentricity, inclined loading, foundation depth, foundation
base on a slope, and a tilted foundation base.

      b. Terzaghi Model. An early approximate solution to bearing capacity was
defined as general shear failure (Terzaghi 1943). The Terzaghi model is applicable
to level strip footings placed on or near a level ground surface where foundation
depth D is less than the minimum width B. Assumptions include use of a surface
footing on soil at plastic equilibrium and a failure surface similar to Figure 1-3a.
Shear resistance of soil above the base of an embedded foundation is not included in
the solution.




                                            4-2
 EM 1110-1-1905
30 Oct 92

      c. Meyerhof Model. This solution considers correction factors for
eccentricity, load inclination, and foundation depth. The influence of the shear
strength of soil above the base of the foundation is considered in this solution.
Therefore, beneficial effects of the foundation depth can be included in the
analysis. Assumptions include use of a shape factor ζ q for surcharge, soil at
plastic equilibrium, and a log spiral failure surface that includes shear above the
base of the foundation. The angle ψ = 45 + φ/2 was used for determination of N γ .
Table 4-3 illustrates the Meyerhof dimensionless bearing capacity and correction
factors required for solution of Equation 4-1 (Meyerhof 1963).

factors in 2-degree intervals.

results.content:
bearing capacity of soil under shallow and deep foundations supporting various types
of structures and embankments. This information is generally applicable to
foundation investigation and design conducted by Corps of Engineer agencies.

      a. Applicability. Principles for evaluating bearing capacity presented in
this manual are applicable to numerous types of structures such as buildings and
houses, towers and storage tanks, fills, embankments and dams. These guidelines may
be helpful in determining soils that will lead to bearing capacity failure or
excessive settlements for given foundations and loads.

      b. Evaluation. Bearing capacity evaluation is presented in Table 1-1.
Consideration should be given to obtaining the services and advice of specialists
and consultants in foundation design where foundation conditions are unusual or
critical or structures are economically significant.

      (1) Definitions, failure modes and factors that influence bearing capacity
are given in Chapter 1.

      (2) Evaluation of bearing capacity can be complicated by environmental and
soil conditions. Some of these non-load related design considerations are given in
Chapter 2.

      (3) Laboratory and in situ methods of determining soil parameters required
for analysis of bearing capacity are given in Chapter 3.

      (4) Analysis of the bearing capacity of shallow foundations is given in
Chapter 4 and of deep foundations is given in Chapter 5.

      c. Limitations. This manual presents estimates of obtaining the bearing
capacity of shallow and deep foundations for certain soil and foundation conditions
using well-established, approximate solutions of bearing capacity.

        (1)   This manual excludes analysis of the bearing capacity of foundations in
rock.

      (2)     This manual excludes analysis of bearing capacity influenced by seismic
forces.

      (3) Refer to EM 1110-2-1902, Stability of Earth and Rockfill Dams, for
solution of the slope stability of embankments.

      d. References. Standard references pertaining to this manual are listed in
Appendix A, References. Each reference is identified in the text by the designated
Government publication number or performing agency. Additional reading materials
are listed in Appendix B, Bibliography.


                                           1-1
 EM 1110-1-1905
30 Oct 92

                                          TABLE 1-1

                                 Bearing Capacity Evaluation


 Step                                       Procedure

   1         Evaluate the ultimate bearing capacity pressure qu   or bearing force    Qu
             using guidelines in this manual and Equation 1-1.

   2         Determine a reasonable factor of safety FS based on available subsurface
             surface information, variability of the soil, soil layering and strengths,
             type and importance of the structure and past experience. FS will
             typically be between 2 and 4. Typical FS are given in Table 1-2.

   3         Evaluate allowable bearing capacity qa by dividing    qu   by FS; i.e., qa =
             qu/FS, Equation 1-2a or Qa = Qu/FS, Equation 1-2b.

   4         Perform settlement analysis when possible and adjust the bearing pressure
             until settlements are within tolerable limits. The resulting design bearing
             pressure qd may be less than qa. Settlement analysis is particularly
             needed when compressible layers are present beneath the depth of the zone
             of a potential bearing failure. Settlement analysis must be performed on
             important structures and those sensitive to settlement. Refer to EM
             1110-1-1904 for settlement analysis of shallow foundations and embankments
             and EM 1110-2-2906, Reese and O’Neill (1988) and Vanikar (1986) for
             settlement of deep foundations.



1-2.    Definitions.

      a. Bearing Capacity. Bearing capacity is the ability of soil to safely carry
the pressure placed on the soil from any engineered structure without undergoing a
shear failure with accompanying large settlements. Applying a bearing pressure
which is safe with respect to failure does not ensure that settlement of the
foundation will be within acceptable limits. Therefore, settlement analysis should
generally be performed since most structures are sensitive to excessive settlement.

      (1) Ultimate Bearing Capacity. The generally accepted method of bearing
capacity analysis is to assume that the soil below the foundation along a critical
plane of failure (slip path) is on the verge of failure and to calculate the bearing
pressure applied by the foundation required to cause this failure condition. This
is the ultimate bearing capacity qu. The general equation is

                                                                                     (1-1a)


where                                                                                (1-1b)

        qu         = ultimate bearing capacity pressure, kips per square foot (ksf)
        Qu         = ultimate bearing capacity force, kips

     B            = foundation width, ft

     Nc,N γ ,Nq = dimensionless bearing capacity factors for cohesion c, soil

     ζ c,ζ γ ,ζ q = dimensionless correction factors for cohesion, soil weight in

A description of factors that influence bearing capacity and calculation of γ’
                                                                             H and
γ’

capacity "N" and correction "ζ" factors are given in Chapter 4 for shallow
foundations and in Chapter 5 for deep foundations.

      (a) Bearing pressures exceeding the limiting shear resistance of the soil
cause collapse of the structure which is usually accompanied by tilting. A bearing
capacity failure results in very large downward movements of the structure,
typically 0.5 ft to over 10 ft in magnitude. A bearing capacity failure of this
type usually occurs within 1 day after the first full load is applied to the soil.

      (b) Ultimate shear failure is seldom a controlling factor in design because
few structures are able to tolerate the rather large deformations that occur in soil
prior to failure. Excessive settlement and differential movement can cause
distortion and cracking in structures, loss of freeboard and water retaining
capacity of embankments and dams, misalignment of operating equipment, discomfort to
occupants, and eventually structural failure. Therefore, settlement analyses must
frequently be performed to establish the expected foundation settlement. Both total
and differential settlement between critical parts of the structure must be compared
with allowable values. Refer to EM 1110-1-1904 for further details.

      (c) Calculation of the bearing pressure required for ultimate shear failure
is useful where sufficient data are not available to perform a settlement analysis.
A suitable safety factor can be applied to the calculated ultimate bearing pressure
where sufficient experience and practice have established appropriate safety
factors. Structures such as embankments and uniformly loaded tanks, silos, and mats
founded on soft soils and designed to tolerate large settlements all may be
susceptible to a base shear failure.

      (2) Allowable Bearing Capacity. The allowable bearing capacity qa is the
ultimate bearing capacity qu divided by an appropriate factor of safety FS,

                                                                                    (1-2a)

                                                                                    (1-2b)




                                          1-3
 EM 1110-1-1905
30 Oct 92

FS is often determined to limit settlements to less than 1 inch and it is often in
the range of 2 to 4.

      (a) Settlement analysis should be performed to determine the maximum vertical
foundation pressures which will keep settlements within the predetermined safe value
for the given structure. The recommended design bearing pressure qd or design
bearing force Qd could be less than qa or Qa due to settlement limitations.

      (b) When practical, vertical pressures applied to supporting foundation soils
which are preconsolidated should be kept less than the maximum past pressure
(preconsolidation load) applied to the soil. This avoids the higher rate of
settlement per unit pressure that occurs on the virgin consolidation settlement
portion of the e-log p curve past the preconsolidation pressure. The e-log p curve
and preconsolidation pressure are determined by performing laboratory consolidation
tests, EM 1110-2-1906.

      (3) Factors of Safety. Table 1-2 illustrates some factors of safety. These
FS’s are conservative and will generally limit settlement to acceptable values, but
economy may be sacrificed in some cases.

      (a) FS selected for design depends on the extent of information available on
subsoil characteristics and their variability. A thorough and extensive subsoil
investigation may permit use of smaller FS.

     (b)   FS    should generally be ≥ 2.5 and never less than 2.

      (c) FS in Table 1-2 for deep foundations are consistent with usual
compression loads. Refer to EM 1110-2-2906 for FS to be used with other loads.

      b. Soil. Soil is a mixture of irregularly shaped mineral particles of
various sizes containing voids between particles. These voids may contain water if

= 4 and for long (L ≈ 5B) rectangular foundations around D/B = 8. The limits of the
types of failure depend upon the compressibility of the sand. More compressible
materials will have lower critical depths (Vesic 1963).


1-4. Factors Influencing Ultimate Bearing Capacity. Principal factors that
influence ultimate bearing capacities are type and strength of soil, foundation
width and depth, soil weight in the shear zone, and surcharge. Structural rigidity
and the contact stress distribution do not greatly influence bearing capacity.
Bearing capacity analysis assumes a uniform contact pressure between the foundation
and underlying soil.

      a. Soil Strength. Many sedimentary soil deposits have an inherent
anisotropic structure due to their common natural deposition in horizontal layers.
Other soil deposits such as saprolites may also exhibit anisotropic properties. The
undrained strength of cohesive soil and friction angle of cohesionless soil will be
influenced by the direction of the major principal stress relative to the direction
of deposition. This manual calculates bearing capacity using strength parameters
determined when the major principal stress is applied in the direction of
deposition.

                                         1-11
                                                                           EM 1110-1-1905
                                                                               30 Oct 92

      c. Foundation Depth. Bearing capacity, particularly that of cohesionless
soil, increases with foundation depth if the soil is uniform. Bearing capacity is
reduced if the foundation is carried down to a weak stratum.

      (1) The bearing capacity of larger footings with a slip path that intersects
a rigid stratum will be greater than that of a smaller footing with a slip path that
does not intersect a deeper rigid stratum, Figure 1-3.

      (2) Foundations placed at depths where the structural weight equals the
weight of displaced soil usually assures adequate bearing capacity and only
recompression settlement. Exceptions include structures supported by
underconsolidated soil and collapsible soil subject to wetting.

      d. Soil Weight and Surcharge. Subsurface and surcharge soil weights
contribute to bearing capacity as given in Equation 1-1. The depth to the water
table influences the subsurface and surcharge soil weights, Figure 1-6. Water table
depth can vary significantly with time.




                       Figure 1-6.   Schematic of foundation system

water table has no influence on the bearing capacity and effective unit weights γ’D
and γ’H in Equation 1-1 are equal to the wet unit weight of the soils γ D and γ H.

      (2) If the water table is above the failure surface and beneath the
foundation base, then the effective unit weight γ’H can be estimated as

      e. Spacing Between Foundations. Foundations on footings spaced sufficiently
close together to intersect adjacent shear zones may decrease bearing capacity of
each foundation. Spacings between footings should be at least 1.5B, to minimize any
reduction in bearing capacity. Increases in settlement of existing facilities
should be checked when placing new construction near existing facilities.

4-11.   Sliding Factor of Safety.

    a. General. Limit equilibrium analysis is used to assess the stability
against sliding. A factor of safety (FS) is applied to the factors which
affect the sliding stability and are known with the least degree of certainty.
These factors are the material strength properties. An FS is applied to the
material strength properties in a manner that places the forces acting on the
structure and soil wedges into equilibrium. Since the in situ strength para-
meters of rock and soil are never known exactly, one role of the FS is to
compensate for the uncertainty that exists in assigning single values to such
important parameters. In other words, the FS compensates for the difference
between what may be the real shear strength and the shear strength assumed for
the analysis.

   b.    Definition.

    (1) A state of limiting equilibrium is said to exist when the applied
shear stresses are equal to the maximum shear strength along a potential fail-
ure surface. Therefore, a structure is stable against sliding along a poten-
tial failure surface when the applied shear stress is less than the available
shear strength along that surface. The ratio of the shear strength to the
applied shear stress along a potential failure surface is defined as the FS ,
as shown in Equation 4-5.

5-5.2.4        Design of Anchors to Resist Hydrostatic Uplift.

Ground anchors may also be used to provide resistance against uplift forces caused by
hydrostatic pressures. Two cases can be considered: 1) the structure is founded on
rock or relatively stiff soil or 2) the structure is founded on relatively compressible soil
with the anchors are secured in deeper soil or rock. When the structure is founded on
rock or suitable soil for anchor development, the calculations presented in Section 5-
5.2.2 and 5-5.2.3 can be used. When a more compressible soil layer exists between
                                                 345
                                                                            UFC 3-220-20
                                                                        16 January 2025


the structure and the anchors, as shown in Figure 5-40, changes in anchor loads
resulting from movement of enclosed compressible ground mass (i.e., groundwater
fluctuations, consolidation settlement or heave, or creep deformations) must be
considered.




Figure 5-40 Resisting Hydrostatic Uplift with Ground Anchors (after FHWA 1999)

The design should verify that the hydrostatic uplift force (U) can be resisted by the
weight of the structure (W1) plus the weight of the enclosed soil mass (W2). The uplift
force should be calculated based on the maximum elevation of the water table. The
buoyant unit weight of soils should be used for soils below the water table. Frictional
resistance is neglected between the soil and walls of the structure. Friction is also
neglected along the hypothetical vertical plane within the soil between the structure and
the top of the bonded zone for the anchor (FHWA 1999).

The anchor loads can change with time. Groundwater fluctuations may cause cyclic
changes in the anchor load. Consolidation and creep may result in detensioning. If any
of these movements could cause additional tension in the tendons after lock-off, the
tendons should be sized accordingly (FHWA 1999).

                                                                          UFC 3-220-20
                                                                      16 January 2025


5-5.2.5      Transient Uplift Loads and Moments on Footings, Piers, and Posts.

Transient uplift and moment loads can be resisted by shallow foundations. Some
simple methods to consider these loadings are presented in Figure 5-41. Design for
moment loading can use methods for rigid retaining walls in Chapter 4. Uplift and
lateral loading of piers, posts, and piles is addressed in more detail in Chapter 6.

5-5.2.6       Uplift Resistance Using a Deadman.

Guidance for the use of a concrete deadman for uplift resistance is provided in Figure
5-42. For a deadman in weak soil, it may be feasible to replace a considerable volume
of soil with granular backfill and construct the block within the new backfill. If this is
done, the passive wedge should be contained entirely within the granular fill, and the
stresses on the remaining weak material should be investigated.




    Figure 5-42 Design Guidance for Uplift Resistance by Concrete Deadman

              DESIGN FOR SPECIAL SOIL CONDITIONS.

              Shallow Foundations on Engineered Fill.

Engineered fill or compacted structural fill can be used to support structures and/or floor
slabs. This fill is designed to have specific strength and compressibility properties and,
as such, must be controlled in the field by personnel under the direction of a
geotechnical engineer. Chapter 3 provides additional detail on fill compaction.

Compacted structural fill is commonly used to raise the general grade for support of a
structure. Structural fill may also be used beneath structures to allow for higher bearing
pressures and reduce settlements by replacing unsuitable foundation soils and/or
providing a relatively stiff mat of soil above less suitable soils.

def load_reactions():
    R = {}
    with open(os.path.join(PROJ, 'structural', 'AV-CR-2604_base_reactions.csv')) as f:
        rows = [r for r in f if not r.startswith('#') and not r.startswith('"#')]
    rd = csv.DictReader(rows)
    for r in rd:
        R.setdefault(r['pad'], {}).setdefault(r['foundation_tag'], {})[r['load_case']] = (
            float(r['P_kips']), float(r['Hx_kips']), float(r['My_kipft']))
    return R

REACT = load_reactions()


def sulfate_class(pct):
    """EM 1110-2-2000 Table 2-2 condition -> UFGS 03 30 00 2.5.2.4 class."""
    if pct < 0.10:
        return 'S0', 'Negligible (< 0.10 %)'
    if pct <= 0.20:
        return 'S1', 'Moderate (0.10 - 0.20 %)'
    if pct <= 2.0:
        return 'S2', 'Severe (> 0.20 %)'
    return 'S3', 'Very severe'

# UFGS 03 30 00 2.5.2 durability tables: (max w/cm or None, min f'c)
DUR = {'F0': (None, 2500), 'F1': (0.55, 3500), 'F2': (0.45, 4500), 'F3': (0.40, 5000),
       'S0': (None, 2500), 'S1': (0.50, 4000), 'S2': (0.45, 4500), 'S3': (0.45, 4500),
       'W0': (None, 2500), 'W1': (0.50, 4000), 'W2': (0.50, 4000),
       'C0': (None, 2500), 'C1': (None, 2500), 'C2': (0.40, 5000)}


def concrete_for_pad(pad):
    sc, _ = sulfate_class(max(SULFATE[pad]))
    classes = [FT_CLASS[pad], sc, W_CLASS, C_CLASS]
    wcm = min(DUR[c][0] for c in classes if DUR[c][0] is not None)
    fcmin = max(DUR[c][1] for c in classes)
    fc = min(s for s in CONC_PRICE if s >= fcmin)
    return dict(classes=classes, sulfate_class=sc, max_wcm=wcm, fc_min=fcmin, fc=fc,
                sulfate_pct=max(SULFATE[pad]))


def base_I(pad, x):
    a, b = BASE_I[pad]
    xx = min(max(x, 0.0), 77.0)       # no extrapolation (adopt nearer boring)
    return round(a + (b - a) * xx / 77.0 + 1e-9, 1)


def strata(pad, x):
    z1 = base_I(pad, x)
    return z1, z1 + THK_II[pad]


def stratum_at(pad, x, depth):
    z1, z2 = strata(pad, x)
    if depth < z1 - 1e-9:
        return 'I'
    if depth < z2 - 1e-9:
        return 'II'
    return 'III'


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- settlement (RFI-019)
def settlement(pad, x, D_ft, B_ft, L_ft, qnet, z_top=0.0, mode='mid'):
    """Layered elastic compression, 2V:1H, 0.25-ft layers, to max(4B,40 ft) below bearing.
    z_top: start of integration below bearing surface (treatment depth for improved case).
    mode 'mid' = Es at layer mid-height; 'split' = layer compliance split at stratum contacts.
    Returns inches."""
    zmax = max(4.0 * min(B_ft, L_ft), 40.0)
    n = int(round(zmax / 0.25))
    z1, z2 = strata(pad, x)
    E = ES[pad]
    s = 0.0
    i0 = int(round(z_top / 0.25))
    for i in range(i0, n):
        zt = i * 0.25
        zm = zt + 0.125
        ds = qnet * B_ft * L_ft / ((B_ft + zm) * (L_ft + zm))
        if mode == 'mid':
            d = D_ft + zm
            st = 'I' if d < z1 else ('II' if d < z2 else 'III')
            s += ds * 0.25 / E[st]
        else:
            a, b = D_ft + zt, D_ft + zt + 0.25
            comp = 0.0
            for lo, hi, st in ((-1e9, z1, 'I'), (z1, z2, 'II'), (z2, 1e9, 'III')):
                h = max(0.0, min(b, hi) - max(a, lo))
                comp += h / E[st]
            s += ds * comp
    return s * 12.0


def top_of_pier_stress(qnet_ksf, Ra, ns=NS):
    return qnet_ksf * ns / (ns * Ra - Ra + 1.0)       # GEC 13 Eq 5-12 (ksf)


def settlement_improved(pad, x, D_ft, B_ft, L_ft, qnet, Ra, Ht, mode='mid'):
    qg = top_of_pier_stress(qnet, Ra)                 # ksf
    suz = (qg * 1000.0 / 144.0) / KG[pad]             # GEC 13 Eq 5-13 (in)
    slz = settlement(pad, x, D_ft, B_ft, L_ft, qnet, z_top=Ht, mode=mode)   # Eq 5-14
    return suz + slz, suz, slz, qg


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- bearing capacity
def _rad(d):
    return d * math.pi / 180.0


def eff_unit_weights(pad, x, D, B):
    """sigma'_zD and average effective unit weight between D and D+B (DM7.2 Fig 5-6)."""
    z1, z2 = strata(pad, x)
    dw = GWT[pad]

    def gam(z):
        st = 'I' if z < z1 else ('II' if z < z2 else 'III')
        g = GAMMA[st]
        return g - GW_UNIT if z >= dw else g
    n = 200
    sig = sum(gam((k + 0.5) * D / n) for k in range(n)) * D / n
    gav = sum(gam(D + (k + 0.5) * B / n) for k in range(n)) / n
    return sig, gav


def qult_all(pad, x, D, B, L):
    st = stratum_at(pad, x, D + 1e-6)
    phi = PHI[st]; c = COH[st]
    p = _rad(phi); t = math.tan(p); s = math.sin(p)
    sig, g = eff_unit_weights(pad, x, D, B)
    BL = B / L
    res = {}
    # Terzaghi (DM7.2 Table 5-2/5-5; Coduto approximation for N_gamma)
    a = math.exp((0.75 * math.pi - p / 2) * t)
    Nq = a * a / (2 * math.cos(math.pi / 4 + p / 2) ** 2)
    Nc = (Nq - 1) / t
    Ng = 2 * (Nq + 1) * t / (1 + 0.4 * math.sin(4 * p))
    sc = 1 + 0.3 * BL; sg = 1 - 0.2 * BL     # interpolate square (1.3, 0.8) to strip (1,1)
    res['Terzaghi'] = c * Nc * sc + sig * Nq + 0.5 * g * B * Ng * sg
    # Meyerhof (DM7.2 Table 5-6)
    Kp = math.tan(math.pi / 4 + p / 2) ** 2
    Nq = Kp * math.exp(math.pi * t)
    Nc = (Nq - 1) / t
    NgM = (Nq - 1) * math.tan(1.4 * p)
    k = D / B
    sc = 1 + 0.2 * BL * Kp; sq = sg = 1 + 0.1 * BL * Kp
    dc = 1 + 0.2 * k * math.sqrt(Kp); dq = dg = 1 + 0.1 * k * math.sqrt(Kp)
    res['Meyerhof'] = c * Nc * sc * dc + sig * Nq * sq * dq + 0.5 * g * B * NgM * sg * dg
    # Brinch Hansen (DM7.2 Table 5-8)
    NgH = 1.5 * (Nq - 1) * t
    kk = k if k < 1 else math.atan(k)
    sc = 1 + BL * (Nq / Nc) * math.cos(p); sq = 1 + s * BL; sg = max(1 - 0.4 * BL, 0.6)
    dq = 1 + 2 * kk * t * (1 - s) ** 2
    dc = 1 + kk * (1 - s) ** 2 * (Nq / Nc)        # as printed in DM7.2 Table 5-8 (conservative)
    res['Brinch Hansen'] = c * Nc * sc * dc + sig * Nq * sq * dq + 0.5 * g * B * NgH * sg
    # Vesic (EM 1110-1-1905 Table 4-6) - for information
    NgV = 2 * (Nq + 1) * t
    sc = 1 + BL * Nq / Nc; sq = 1 + BL * t; sg = max(1 - 0.4 * BL, 0.6)
    dc = 1 + 0.4 * kk; dq = 1 + 2 * kk * t * (1 - s) ** 2
    res['Vesic'] = c * Nc * sc * dc + sig * Nq * sq * dq + 0.5 * g * B * NgV * sg
    return res, sig, g, st


def q_allow_net(pad, x, D, B, L):
    res, sig, g, st = qult_all(pad, x, D, B, L)
    fs = FS_TABLE[OCC[pad]]
    m = min(res['Terzaghi'], res['Meyerhof'], res['Brinch Hansen'])
    return m / fs - sig, res, sig, g, st     # DM7.2 Eq 5-14


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structural
def shear_ok(Pu, B_in, L_in, c1, c2, t_in, fc, phi=0.75, wall=False):
    d = t_in - 4.0
    if d <= 0:
        return False
    A = B_in * L_in
    qu = Pu * 1000.0 / A                      # psi
    rf = math.sqrt(fc)
    # one-way, bars spanning B (critical section at d from face, across full L)
    proj = (B_in - c1) / 2.0 - d
    if proj > 0 and qu * L_in * proj > phi * 2 * rf * L_in * d:
        return False
    proj = (L_in - c2) / 2.0 - d
    if proj > 0 and qu * B_in * proj > phi * 2 * rf * B_in * d:
        return False
    # two-way at d/2 when perimeter lies inside the footing
    if (c1 + d) < B_in and (c2 + d) < L_in:
        b0 = 2 * (c1 + d) + 2 * (c2 + d)
        Vu = Pu * 1000.0 * (1 - (c1 + d) * (c2 + d) / A)
        beta = max(c1, c2) / min(c1, c2)
        vc = min(4.0, 2 + 4.0 / beta, 2 + 40.0 * d / b0) * rf
        if Vu > phi * vc * b0 * d:
            return False
    return True


def thickness_req(Pu, B_in, L_in, c1, c2, fc, phi=0.75, wall=False):
    t = 12.0
    while not shear_ok(Pu, B_in, L_in, c1, c2, t, fc, phi, wall):
        t += 3.0
        if t > 120:
            return None
    return t


def flexure_rho(Pu, B_in, L_in, c1, c2, t_in, fc):
    """Required gross steel ratio (each direction, governing) for cantilever flexure at face."""
    d = t_in - 4.0
    qu = Pu * 1000.0 / (B_in * L_in)
    out = 0.0
    for span, width, c in ((B_in, L_in, c1), (L_in, B_in, c2)):
        arm = (span - c) / 2.0
        if arm <= 0:
            continue
        Mu = qu * width * arm * arm / 2.0     # lb-in
        # As from phi*As*fy*(d - a/2) = Mu, a = As fy/(0.85 fc b)
        phi = 0.9
        Rn = Mu / (phi * width * d * d)
        disc = 1 - 2 * Rn / (0.85 * fc)
        if disc <= 0:
            return None
        rho_d = 0.85 * fc / FY * (1 - math.sqrt(disc))
        As = rho_d * width * d
        out = max(out, As / (width * t_in))
    return out


BARS = {4: 0.20, 5: 0.31, 6: 0.44, 7: 0.60, 8: 0.79, 9: 1.00, 10: 1.27, 11: 1.56}
BAR_DIA = {4: 0.5, 5: 0.625, 6: 0.75, 7: 0.875, 8: 1.0, 9: 1.128, 10: 1.27, 11: 1.41}


def choose_bars(rho_target, t_in):
    """Bar size and spacing (<= 12 in, whole inches >= 6 in) with provided gross ratio >= target,
    minimising the provided ratio."""
    best = None
    for bar, ab in BARS.items():
        for s in range(12, 5, -1):
            rho = ab * 12.0 / s / (12.0 * t_in)
            if rho >= rho_target - 1e-12:
                if best is None or rho < best[2] - 1e-12:
                    best = (bar, s, rho)
                break
    return best


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- quantities / cost
def excavation_cf(B_ft, L_ft, D_ft):
    a = B_ft + 2.0; b = L_ft + 2.0
    if D_ft <= 4.0 + 1e-9:
        return a * b * D_ft
    s = 1.5
    return a * b * D_ft + (a + b) * s * D_ft ** 2 + (4.0 / 3.0) * s * s * D_ft ** 3


def dewater_days(pad, D_ft):
    if D_ft <= GWT[pad] + 1e-9:
        return 0
    return int(math.ceil(3.0 * (D_ft - GWT[pad]) - 1e-9))

"""Candidate generation + chain DP (angular distortion) + campus rig selection."""
import math, json, sys, pickle
import numpy as np
from core import *

GRID = 0.25  # ft (3 in)


def unit_profile(pad, x, D, B, L):
    """Per-layer compression for unit net pressure (in per ksf), mid and split modes.
    Returns (cum_mid, cum_split) where cum[k] = sum of layers from index k to end."""
    zmax = max(4.0 * min(B, L), 40.0)
    n = int(round(zmax / 0.25))
    zt = np.arange(n) * 0.25
    zm = zt + 0.125
    infl = B * L / ((B + zm) * (L + zm))
    z1, z2 = strata(pad, x)
    E = ES[pad]
    d = D + zm
    Em = np.where(d < z1, E['I'], np.where(d < z2, E['II'], E['III']))
    lay_mid = infl * 0.25 / Em * 12.0
    a = D + zt; b = a + 0.25
    comp = np.zeros(n)
    for lo, hi, st in ((-1e9, z1, 'I'), (z1, z2, 'II'), (z2, 1e9, 'III')):
        h = np.clip(np.minimum(b, hi) - np.maximum(a, lo), 0, None)
        comp += h / E[st]
    lay_split = infl * comp * 12.0
    cm = np.concatenate([np.cumsum(lay_mid[::-1])[::-1], [0.0]])
    cs = np.concatenate([np.cumsum(lay_split[::-1])[::-1], [0.0]])
    return cm, cs


def piers_fit(B, L):
    """Max number of 30-in piers wholly inside a B x L footprint at >= 3.5 ft c/c."""
    p = PIER_PITCH; r = PIER_D_IN / 24.0
    best = 0
    for (bb, ll) in ((B, L), (L, B)):
        if bb < 2 * r or ll < 2 * r:
            continue
        nx = int(math.floor((bb - 2 * r) / p + 1e-9)) + 1
        ny = int(math.floor((ll - 2 * r) / p + 1e-9)) + 1
        best = max(best, nx * ny)
        # staggered: rows along ll spaced p*sin60, alternate rows offset p/2 along bb
        dy = p * math.sqrt(3) / 2
        nrows = int(math.floor((ll - 2 * r) / dy + 1e-9)) + 1
        n_full = nx
        n_off = int(math.floor((bb - 2 * r - p / 2) / p + 1e-9)) + 1 if bb - 2 * r >= p / 2 else 0
        tot = sum(n_full if k % 2 == 0 else n_off for k in range(nrows))
        best = max(best, tot)
    return best


def sliding_etc(pad, B, L, t, D):
    """Shear-wall footing stability (conservative evaluation). B, L, t, D in ft."""
    r = REACT[pad]['W1']
    P06, H06, M06 = r['0.6D_PLUS_W']
    U = -r['UPLIFT_W'][0]
    Pd = r['DEAD_ONLY'][0]
    Pw, Hw, Mw = r['SERVICE_D_PLUS_L_PLUS_W']
    Wf = B * L * t * CONC_PCF / 1000.0
    Ws = max(D - t, 0.0) * (B * L - (WALL_T_IN / 12.0) * WALL_L_FT) * GAMMA['I']
    st = 'I'
    phi = PHI[st]; c = COH[st]
    delta = math.radians(2.0 / 3.0 * phi)
    N = P06 - U + 0.6 * (Wf + Ws)           # 0.6D + W including wind uplift (conservative)
    Kp = math.tan(math.radians(45 + phi / 2.0)) ** 2
    top = D - t
    Pp = B * (0.5 * Kp * GAMMA['I'] * (D ** 2 - top ** 2) + 2 * c * math.sqrt(Kp) * t)
    fs_slide = (N * math.tan(delta) + 0.5 * Pp) / H06
    # alternative (less conservative) definition for information
    N2 = P06 + 0.6 * (Wf + Ws)
    fs_slide_alt = (N2 * math.tan(delta) + 0.5 * Pp) / H06
    e_ft = (Mw + Hw * t) / (Pw + Wf + Ws)
    e_rep_ft = (Mw + Hw * D) / Pw                 # reported (conservative)
    fs_uplift = 0.6 * (Wf + Ws + Pd) / U
    return dict(fs_slide=fs_slide, fs_slide_alt=fs_slide_alt, e_ft=e_ft, e_rep_ft=e_rep_ft,
                fs_uplift=fs_uplift, N=N, Pp=Pp, Wf=Wf, Ws=Ws, mu=math.tan(delta))


def gen_candidates(pad, tag, D_in, phi_v=0.75, Bmax_ft=40.0, s_lim=0.97, allow_imp=True,
                   wall_L_opts=None):
    D = D_in / 12.0
    x = STATION[tag]
    conc = concrete_for_pad(pad)
    fc = conc['fc']
    P = REACT[pad][tag]['SERVICE_D_PLUS_L'][0]
    Pu = REACT[pad][tag]['STRENGTH_1.2D_1.6L'][0]
    wall = tag == 'W1'
    if wall:
        c1, c2 = WALL_T_IN, WALL_L_FT * 12.0
        Bmin_in = 21.0
        Ls = wall_L_opts or [288.0, 300.0, 312.0, 324.0, 336.0]
    else:
        c1 = c2 = COL_IN[tag]
        Bmin_in = 24.0
        Ls = None
    cands = []
    Bin = Bmin_in
    while Bin <= Bmax_ft * 12 + 1e-6:
        Lopts = Ls if wall else [Bin]
        for Lin in Lopts:
            if Lin < Bin and not wall:
                continue
            B = Bin / 12.0; L = Lin / 12.0
            t_req = thickness_req(Pu, Bin, Lin, c1, c2, fc, phi_v)
            if t_req is None or t_req >= D_in:
                continue
            tops = [t_req]
            if wall:
                tops = [t_req + 3 * k for k in range(0, 5) if t_req + 3 * k < D_in]
            qa, res, sig, g, st = q_allow_net(pad, x, D, B, L)
            cm, cs = unit_profile(pad, x, D, B, L)
            for t_in in tops:
                t = t_in / 12.0
                qnet = P / (B * L) + (CONC_PCF / 1000.0 - GAMMA['I']) * t
                if qnet > qa:
                    continue
                rho_req = flexure_rho(Pu, Bin, Lin, c1, c2, t_in, fc)
                if rho_req is None:
                    continue
                bar = choose_bars(max(RHO_MIN, rho_req), t_in)
                if bar is None:
                    continue
                stab = None
                if wall:
                    stab = sliding_etc(pad, B, L, t, D)
                    if stab['fs_slide'] < FS_SLIDING or stab['fs_uplift'] < FS_UPLIFT:
                        continue
                    if stab['e_ft'] > min(L, B) / 6.0 or stab['e_rep_ft'] > min(L, B) / 6.0:
                        continue
                Vc = B * L * t
                conc_cost = Vc / 27.0 * CONC_PRICE[fc]
                steel_cost = 2 * bar[2] * Vc * STEEL_PCF * REBAR_PRICE
                Vx = excavation_cf(B, L, D)
                exc_cost = Vx / 27.0 * EXC_PRICE + (Vx - Vc) / 27.0 * BKF_PRICE
                base = dict(pad=pad, tag=tag, B_in=Bin, L_in=Lin, t_in=t_in, t_req=t_req, qnet=qnet,
                            qa=qa, qult=res, st=st, rho_req=rho_req, bar=bar, stab=stab,
                            conc_cost=conc_cost, steel_cost=steel_cost, exc_cost=exc_cost,
                            Vc=Vc, Vx=Vx)
                # spread
                s_mid = qnet * cm[0]; s_spl = qnet * cs[0]
                if max(s_mid, s_spl) <= s_lim:
                    c = dict(base); c.update(type='SPREAD', s=s_mid, s_split=s_spl, n=0, Ht=0, Ra=0.0,
                                             qg=0.0, pier_cost=0.0, plat_cost=0.0,
                                             cost=conc_cost + steel_cost + exc_cost)
                    cands.append(c)
                if not allow_imp:
                    continue
                nfit = piers_fit(B, L)
                nmin = int(math.ceil(RA_MIN * B * L / PIER_AREA - 1e-9))
                nmax = min(nfit, int(math.floor(0.40 * B * L / PIER_AREA + 1e-9)))
                if nmin > nmax:
                    continue
                kgp = KG[pad]
                for n in range(nmin, min(nmax, nmin + 6) + 1):
                    Ra = n * PIER_AREA / (B * L)
                    qg = top_of_pier_stress(qnet, Ra)
                    if qg * 1000.0 > QG_MAX_PSF:
                        continue
                    suz = qg * 1000.0 / 144.0 / kgp
                    for Ht in range(TREAT_MIN, TREAT_MAX + 1):
                        k = int(round(Ht / 0.25))
                        if k >= len(cm):
                            break
                        s_mid = suz + qnet * cm[k]; s_spl = suz + qnet * cs[k]
                        if max(s_mid, s_spl) > s_lim:
                            continue
                        pc = n * Ht * PIER_LF
                        plc = B * L / 9.0 * PLATFORM_SY
                        c = dict(base); c.update(type='IMPROVED_SPREAD', s=s_mid, s_split=s_spl, n=n,
                                                 Ht=Ht, Ra=Ra, qg=qg, suz=suz, pier_cost=pc,
                                                 plat_cost=plc,
                                                 cost=conc_cost + steel_cost + exc_cost + pc + plc)
                        cands.append(c)
        Bin += 3.0
    return cands


def prune(cands, res=0.002):
    """Keep cheapest candidate per settlement bin (bins on s_mid; track split too)."""
    best = {}
    for c in cands:
        key = (int(math.floor(c['s'] / res)), c['type'] == 'IMPROVED_SPREAD')
        if key not in best or c['cost'] < best[key]['cost']:
            best[key] = c
    return list(best.values())


def chain_dp(cand_lists, margin=0.01, imp_mode='any'):
    """cand_lists: list over TAGS of candidate lists. Minimise total cost s.t. adjacent
    |s_i - s_j| <= dist/500 - margin (checked on both mid and split settlements).
    imp_mode: 'any' (no restriction), 'none' (no improved allowed)."""
    order = TAGS
    lists = []
    for tag, cl in zip(order, cand_lists):
        if imp_mode == 'none':
            cl = [c for c in cl if c['type'] == 'SPREAD']
        lists.append(cl)
    if any(len(l) == 0 for l in lists):
        return None
    # DP
    prev = [(c['cost'], None) for c in lists[0]]
    back = [None]
    for i in range(1, len(order)):
        lim = (STATION[order[i]] - STATION[order[i - 1]]) * 12.0 * ANG_LIMIT - margin
        A = lists[i - 1]; Bl = lists[i]
        sA = np.array([c['s'] for c in A]); sA2 = np.array([c['s_split'] for c in A])
        costA = np.array([p[0] for p in prev])
        cur = []; bk = []
        for c in Bl:
            ok = (np.abs(sA - c['s']) <= lim) & (np.abs(sA2 - c['s_split']) <= lim)
            if not ok.any():
                cur.append((math.inf, None)); bk.append(None); continue
            cc = np.where(ok, costA, np.inf)
            j = int(np.argmin(cc))
            cur.append((cc[j] + c['cost'], j)); bk.append(j)
        prev = cur
        back.append(bk)
    costs = np.array([p[0] for p in prev])
    j = int(np.argmin(costs))
    if not np.isfinite(costs[j]):
        return None
    sel = [None] * len(order)
    sel[-1] = j
    for i in range(len(order) - 1, 0, -1):
        sel[i - 1] = back[i][sel[i]]
    design = [lists[i][sel[i]] for i in range(len(order))]
    return float(costs[j]), design


def pad_fixed(pad, D_in, design):
    days = dewater_days(pad, D_in / 12.0)
    imp = any(c['type'] == 'IMPROVED_SPREAD' for c in design)
    return days * DEWATER_DAY + (MOD_TEST if imp else 0.0), days, imp

5.3.1 Serviceability Criteria

The tolerable movements a structure can withstand depend on the type of structure, the expected
service life and the consequences of excessive movements. Tolerable movements are frequently
described in terms of angular distortion between members. “Angular distortion” is defined as the
ratio of the differential settlement (δ') between footings to the span length (l), or δ'/l. The
maximum angular distortion should be limited to some acceptable value to minimize structural
strength and serviceability problems. Excessive differential displacements can induce significant
structural cracking.

Empirical studies of the performance of bridges subjected to various maximum angular
distortions between adjacent foundations concluded that the serviceability criteria would be met
if the angular distortion for simple span bridges is less than 0.005 and, for continuous span
bridges, less than 0.004 (Moulton et al., 1982, 1985). Using these criteria, a continuous span
bridge having a span length of 30 m (100 ft) can tolerate a differential settlement of about 130
mm (5 in) between supports. In practice, bridges are typically designed for tolerable settlements
much smaller than this. It is not uncommon for continuous span structures to be designed for
differential settlements between adjacent piers of about 25 mm (1 in) or less, and for simply
supported spans of about 38 to 50 mm (1½ to 2 in).

DiMillio (1982) reports in the FHWA research report “Performance of Highway Abutments on
Spread Footings” that moderate differential movements of 25 to 75 mm (1 to 3 in) caused very

                                                 73
 little distress in any of the structures studied. Of the 148 bridges with spread footings studied,
the foundation movements observed were small, and the movements did not cause significant
distress.

For large footings on non-uniform soil profiles, or footings subjected to large eccentric loads,
footing rotation may be a concern. In these cases the magnitude of the rotation can be computed
by considering the potential differential settlement due to the difference in the applied loads or
the non-uniformity of the soil profile.

It should be noted that tolerable differential movement between adjacent columns within a single
pier or bent may be significantly smaller than between adjacent piers on the same structure due
to the rigidity and relatively short length of the superstructure cross beam. The geotechnical and
structural engineers should confer when there is potential for adjacent individual spread footings
supporting columns within the same pier to experience differential settlements.

In some situations, the total movements may be the criteria that are critical in ensuring that
serviceability issues are met. An example might be a simply supported, single-span structure
with predicted settlements of several tenths of a meter at both abutments. While the structure
itself is not at structural or performance risk due to the total, but relatively uniform movements,
the resulting sag in the roadway profile may be unacceptable for vehicle ride, safety or aesthetic


8.3 ALLOWABLE BEARING STRESSES

8.3.1 Settlement Limitations

Tolerable total and differential movements for buildings, like bridges, are strongly a function of
the materials and methods used to construct the building. Steel frame buildings are capable of
withstanding surprisingly large differential movements without experiencing structural distress
or damage. However, such movement may result in objectionable appearances of wall facings
and coverings. Masonry structures, on the other hand, are relatively settlement intolerant and
may experience structural distress (cracking) if angular distortions exceed 1/300.

In practice, bearing stresses are typically limited so that total settlements are on the order of 25
mm (1 in) and differential settlements about half the total settlement.

In designing building foundations, considerable benefits can be derived by permanently
excavating a portion of the soil by including a basement. This reduces the net increase in
stresses on the subgrade, which in turn reduces or eliminates consolidation even in normally
consolidated soils.

arguments.content:
"""Build reported values for every foundation + pad, and write JSON deliverables."""
import json, math, pickle, os, sys
from finalize import *

OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, 'output', 'stage')
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

ALT = json.load(open('alternatives.json')) if os.path.exists('alternatives.json') else {}


def build():
    results = pickle.load(open('final_designs.pkl', 'rb'))
    pads_improved = [p for p in PADS if results[p]['imp']]
    nrig = int(math.ceil(len(pads_improved) / PADS_PER_RIG))
    mob = nrig * MOB_RIG
    rep = {}
    for pad in PADS:
        R = results[pad]
        D_in = R['D_in']; des = R['des']
        conc = concrete_for_pad(pad)
        fnd = {}
        govs = []
        for i, c in enumerate(des):
            tag = c['tag']
            g, viol = governing_for(pad, D_in, des, i)
            govs.append(g)
            e = evaluate(pad, tag, D_in, c['B_in'], c['L_in'], c['t_in'], c['type'], c['n'], c['Ht'])
            e2 = evaluate(pad, tag, D_in, c['B_in'], c['L_in'], c['t_in'], c['type'], c['n'], c['Ht'], 'P/A')
            s_rep = ceil_to(max(e['s_mid'], e['s_split']), 3)
            d = dict(
                foundation_type=c['type'], B_in=int(c['B_in']), L_in=int(c['L_in']), thickness_in=int(c['t_in']),
                bearing_stratum=e['st'], reinforcement_ratio=round(c['bar'][2], 6), bar_size=int(c['bar'][0]),
                bar_spacing_in=int(c['bar'][1]), q_net_ksf=ceil_to(e['q'], 3), q_allow_net_ksf=floor_to(e['qa'], 3),
                settlement_in=s_rep,
                pier_count=int(c['n']) if c['type'] != 'SPREAD' else 0,
                pier_diameter_in=int(PIER_D_IN) if c['type'] != 'SPREAD' else 0,
                pier_depth_ft=int(c['Ht']) if c['type'] != 'SPREAD' else 0,
                area_replacement_ratio=floor_to(e['Ra'], 4) if c['type'] != 'SPREAD' else 0.0,
                top_of_pier_stress_psf=float(math.ceil(e['qg'] * 1000.0)) if c['type'] != 'SPREAD' else 0.0,
                governing_constraint=g)
            if tag == 'W1':
                st = sliding_etc(pad, c['B_in'] / 12, c['L_in'] / 12, c['t_in'] / 12, D_in / 12)
                d['sliding_fs'] = floor_to(st['fs_slide'], 2)
                d['eccentricity_in'] = ceil_to(st['e_rep_ft'] * 12, 2)
                d['uplift_fs'] = floor_to(st['fs_uplift'], 2)
            fnd[tag] = d
            c['_eval'] = e; c['_eval_PA'] = e2; c['_viol'] = viol; c['_gov'] = g
        pg = pad_governing(pad, D_in, des, govs)
        rep[pad] = dict(
            bearing_depth_in=int(D_in), fs_bearing=FS_TABLE[OCC[pad]], occupancy_class=OCC[pad],
            improved=bool(R['imp']), sulfate_pct=conc['sulfate_pct'], sulfate_exposure_class=conc['sulfate_class'],
            exposure_classes=conc['classes'], fc_psi=int(conc['fc']), max_wcm=conc['max_wcm'],
            dewatering_days=int(R['days']), governing_constraint=pg, foundations=fnd)
    total = sum(results[p]['cost'] + results[p]['fixed'] for p in PADS) + mob
    total = round(total, 2)
    geom = {'project': {'campus_total_cost_usd': total, 'frost_depth_in': FROST_DEPTH_IN,
                        'afi_100yr_F_days': AFI_100},
            'pads': rep}
    # ground improvement plan
    rigs = {}
    for k in range(nrig):
        rigs['RIG-%d' % (k + 1)] = pads_improved[k * PADS_PER_RIG:(k + 1) * PADS_PER_RIG]
    gip = {'stress_concentration_ratio_ns': NS, 'pier_diameter_in': int(PIER_D_IN),
           'rigs_mobilised': nrig, 'mobilisation_cost_usd': float(mob), 'pads_improved': pads_improved,
           'rig_assignments': rigs, 'modulus_tests': {p: 1 for p in pads_improved}, 'pads': {}}
    for p in pads_improved:
        des = results[p]['des']
        imp = [c for c in des if c['type'] != 'SPREAD']
        gip['pads'][p] = {'stiffness_modulus_pci': KG[p], 'treatment_depth_ft': int(max(c['Ht'] for c in imp)),
                          'total_pier_lf': float(sum(c['n'] * c['Ht'] for c in imp))}
    return geom, gip, results, total, nrig, mob, pads_improved


if __name__ == '__main__':
    geom, gip, results, total, nrig, mob, pims = build()
    json.dump(geom, open(os.path.join(OUT, 'foundation_geometry.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    json.dump(gip, open(os.path.join(OUT, 'ground_improvement_plan.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    pickle.dump((geom, gip, results, total, nrig, mob, pims), open('report_state.pkl', 'wb'))
    print('total', total, 'rigs', nrig, pims)
    for p in PADS:
        print(p, geom['pads'][p]['governing_constraint'], [ (t, f['governing_constraint']) for t, f in geom['pads'][p]['foundations'].items()])

"""Write schedule / register xlsx, feasibility matrix and design basis md, and zip the submission."""
import json, os, pickle, zipfile, shutil, math
import openpyxl
from finalize import *
from register_rows import rows as reg_rows

STAGE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'output', 'stage')
geom, gip, results, total, nrig, mob, pims = pickle.load(open('report_state.pkl', 'rb'))
ALT = json.load(open('alternatives.json'))


def money(v):
    return '${:,.0f}'.format(v)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ schedule
def write_schedule():
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(PROJ, 'owner', 'AV-CR-2604_foundation_schedule_TEMPLATE.xlsx'))
    ws = wb['FOUNDATION SCHEDULE']
    hdr = [c.value for c in ws[1]]
    # clear any rows below header
    for r in range(ws.max_row, 1, -1):
        ws.delete_rows(r)
    for pad in PADS:
        P = geom['pads'][pad]
        for tag in TAGS:
            f = P['foundations'][tag]
            rowv = {'pad': pad, 'foundation_tag': tag, 'bearing_depth_in': P['bearing_depth_in'],
                    'fc_psi': P['fc_psi'], 'max_wcm': P['max_wcm']}
            rowv.update(f)
            ws.append([rowv.get(h) for h in hdr])
    wb.save(os.path.join(STAGE, 'foundation_schedule.xlsx'))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ register
def write_register():
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(PROJ, 'owner', 'constraint_register_template.xlsx'))
    ws = wb['CONSTRAINT REGISTER']
    for r in range(ws.max_row, 1, -1):
        ws.delete_rows(r)
    R = reg_rows({})
    n_sub = sum(1 for r in R if r[5] != 'SET ASIDE')
    for i, r in enumerate(R):
        doc, clause, req, val, unit, kind, app, res = r
        ws.append(['R%03d' % (i + 1), doc, clause, req, val if val is not None else '', unit, kind, app, res])
    wb.save(os.path.join(STAGE, 'constraint_register.xlsx'))
    return len(R), n_sub


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ feasibility matrix
def standalone_alternatives(pad, D_in, tag):
    """Cheapest stand-alone spread and improved candidates (individual checks only)."""
    cands = gen_candidates(pad, tag, D_in, Bmax_ft=34.0, allow_imp=True, wall_L_opts=WALL_LS)
    cands = [c for c in cands if c['qnet'] <= c['qa'] - 0.002]
    sp = [c for c in cands if c['type'] == 'SPREAD']
    im = [c for c in cands if c['type'] != 'SPREAD']
    b_sp = min(sp, key=lambda c: c['cost']) if sp else None
    b_im = min(im, key=lambda c: c['cost']) if im else None
    return b_sp, b_im


def write_matrix():
    L = []
    L.append('# Foundation-type feasibility and optimisation matrix - Cattail Run Data Campus, Phase 1 (AV-CR-2604)\n')
    L.append('Units: kips, ksf, in, ft, USD at the project budget unit prices (BoD Rev 3 sec. 5; bid schedule Rev 1; '
             'Kettleridge KGS-26-0917). Demand = SERVICE_D_PLUS_L (bearing, settlement) and STRENGTH_1.2D_1.6L (shear, flexure) '
             'per the load-combination memo. q_net = P/(BL) + (150 - 118 pcf) t. q_allow,net = least of Terzaghi, Meyerhof and '
             'Brinch Hansen (UFC 3-220-20 5-3.3, Eq. 5-15) / FS (UFC 3-220-01 Table 2-3) - sigma\'zD (Eq. 5-14), groundwater-corrected '
             '(Fig. 5-6). Settlement = layered elastic compression (RFI-019; GEC 13 Eq. 5-14), plus qg/kg upper zone for improved '
             'footings (GEC 13 Eq. 5-12/5-13). Angular distortion limit 1/500 between adjacent units (UFC 3-220-01 2-4.7.1). '
             'Stand-alone alternative costs are the cheapest individually-compliant spread and improved-spread design for that '
             'unit at the pad bearing depth (pad-level chain constraints not applied); the pad-level costs are the optimised '
             'whole-pad programmes that decided the pad.\n')
    L.append('Campus programme: improved pads %s; %d rig(s) mobilised (%s); mobilisation %s; campus total %s.\n' % (
        ', '.join(pims), nrig, '; '.join('%s: %s' % (k, ', '.join(v)) for k, v in gip['rig_assignments'].items()),
        money(mob), money(total)))
    for pad in PADS:
        R = results[pad]; P = geom['pads'][pad]; D_in = R['D_in']; des = R['des']
        conc = concrete_for_pad(pad)
        alt = ALT[pad]
        L.append('\n## %s - %s\n' % (pad, BUILDING[pad]))
        L.append('- Occupancy: %s; FS on bearing %.1f (UFC 3-220-01 Table 2-3). Bearing depth %d in (frost minimum 42 in); '
                 'stabilised groundwater %.1f ft; dewatering %d days.' % (OCC[pad], P['fs_bearing'], D_in, GWT[pad], R['days']))
        L.append('- Concrete: f\'c %d psi, max w/cm %.2f (classes %s; sulfate %.3f %% -> %s).' % (
            conc['fc'], conc['max_wcm'], ', '.join(conc['classes']), conc['sulfate_pct'], conc['sulfate_class']))
        L.append('- Stratum I base at stations 0/24/44/60/72/77 ft: %s ft; Stratum II %.1f ft thick; Es I/II/III = %d/%d/%d ksf.' % (
            '/'.join('%.1f' % base_I(pad, STATION[t]) for t in TAGS), THK_II[pad], ES[pad]['I'], ES[pad]['II'], ES[pad]['III']))
        L.append('- Pad governing constraint: **%s**. Decision: **%s**.' % (
            P['governing_constraint'], 'IMPROVED_SPREAD' if R['imp'] else 'SPREAD'))
        L.append('- Pad alternatives (whole-pad optimised, incl. dewatering and modulus test, excl. campus mobilisation): '
                 'spread-only %s (%s); improved %s (%s). Selected: %s.\n' % (
                     money(alt['spread_only_cost_usd']), alt.get('spread_desc', ''), money(alt['improved_cost_usd']),
                     alt.get('improved_desc', ''), 'IMPROVED_SPREAD' if R['imp'] else 'SPREAD'))
        L.append('| Tag | Sta (ft) | P svc / Pu (k) | Type | B x L x t (in) | Stratum | q_net (ksf) | q_allow,net (ksf) | q/qa | '
                 'Settlement (in) | Ang. dist. to next | Piers n x depth (ft), Ra, qg (psf) | Reinf. | Governing | '
                 'Stand-alone spread cost | Stand-alone improved cost | Selected cost |')
        L.append('|' + '---|' * 17)
        for i, c in enumerate(des):
            tag = c['tag']; f = P['foundations'][tag]
            Psvc = REACT[pad][tag]['SERVICE_D_PLUS_L'][0]; Pu = REACT[pad][tag]['STRENGTH_1.2D_1.6L'][0]
            if i + 1 < len(des):
                o = des[i + 1]
                dist = (STATION[des[i + 1]['tag']] - STATION[tag]) * 12.0
                ad = max(abs(c['s'] - o['s']), abs(c['s_split'] - o['s_split'])) / dist
                adtxt = '1/%d (%s-%s)' % (int(1 / ad) if ad > 0 else 99999, tag, o['tag'])
            else:
                adtxt = '-'

# Design basis - Phase 1 foundation strategy, Cattail Run Data Campus (AV-CR-2604)

Structural engineer of record, Phase 1 foundation package. Six pads (CR-P1 to CR-P6), each with one instrumented column line of five isolated column footings (F1-F5) and one continuous shear-wall footing (W1). Every number below is derived from the documents in the data room; the deliverables foundation_geometry.json, ground_improvement_plan.json, foundation_schedule.xlsx, foundation_feasibility_matrix.md and constraint_register.xlsx carry the same values.

## 1. Governing criteria and documents set aside

The criteria that govern are: UFC 3-220-01 Geotechnical Engineering (1 Nov 2012, Change 3, 1 Jul 2025) for bearing, factors of safety (Table 2-3), settlement limits, minimum widths and depth, frost and presumptive-value prohibition; UFC 3-301-01 Structural Engineering (2023, Change 4) for load combinations (2-4.3) and thick-footing reinforcement (1808.8.2.1); UFGS 03 30 00 paragraph 2.5.2 for the concrete exposure-class limits; the Loudoun County AHJ letter LC-BD-26-0774 (Amendment 3 frost depth, Amendment 4 no presumptive values); the Basis of Design Rev 3; the Geotechnical Data Report Rev 2 with its boring logs and laboratory summary; the civil grading and groundwater record; the load-combination memo; the RFI log; the Kettleridge proposal KGS-26-0917 for pier parameters, prices and the mobilisation rule; and the BIM parameter standard Rev 2. The analysis references applied are UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2, 2025) chapter 5 for bearing capacity and its sections 4-5.1.2/4-5.1.3 and Figure 5-41 for wall stability, EM 1110-1-1905 for the bearing-capacity cross-check and groundwater adjustment, FHWA GEC 13 chapter 5 for rammed aggregate piers and the elastic settlement equation, EM 1110-2-2502 for the sliding limit-equilibrium procedure, EM 1110-2-2104 for reinforced-concrete strength (shear per paragraph 5.1) and EM 1110-2-2000 Table 2-2 for the sulfate exposure condition.

Documents reviewed and set aside, with the reason:

- UFC 3-220-01N Foundation Design (2005) and UFC 3-220-10N Soil Mechanics (2005) were set aside because they are cancelled predecessor volumes; UFC 3-220-01 (2012, Change 3) and UFC 3-220-20 (2025) replace them.
- Geotechnical Addendum 1 was set aside because it is superseded in its entirety by Data Report Rev 2 (its Es values of 320/900/2400 ksf and its 4,000 psf presumptive value are withdrawn).
- Basis of Design Rev 1 was set aside because Rev 3 supersedes it (Rev 1 classified every building as Warehouse with F0 concrete, allowed 1-in dimensions and 20 ft depth).
- The NOAA NCEI 1951-1980 air-freezing-index tables were set aside because the AHJ letter Amendment 3 and RFI-007 name them the superseded edition of the product.
- The Broadview Commons adjacent-parcel report (5,500 psf) was set aside because it is a different property with different stratigraphy (RFI-013).
- FHWA GEC 6 (shallow foundations for bridges) was set aside because it is written for a different class of structure; its bridge movement criteria are not used.
- EM 1110-2-2104 Table 3-1 load factors were set aside because they are for hydraulic structures and the load-combination memo states they do not apply.
- The 3,000 psf presumptive value of Data Report Rev 2 section 7 and all building-code presumptive values were set 
....
## 6. Campus programme

Spread footings alone cannot meet the 1 in total-settlement limit on the soft Stratum I residuum of CR-P1, CR-P2 and CR-P6 (Es 85-110 ksf, 6-14 ft thick) at a frost-depth bearing level: the cheapest spread-only programmes found require bearing in Stratum II at 10 ft with dewatering and 1.5H:1V excavations, or footings up to 64 ft wide (about $213,000-$268,000 per pad). Rammed aggregate piers under bearing-sized footings reduce each of those pads to about $84,000-$91,000 including the modulus test. CR-P4 is also improved: its spread-only programme costs $59,746 against $47,725 improved, and because three pads are already improved its share of a rig is free (a rig serves two pads). CR-P3 and CR-P5 stay on spread footings: their stiffer Stratum I (210 and 250 ksf) meets the settlement limits with bearing-sized footings, and improving either would cost more ($56,874 and $38,679 improved versus $33,166 and $19,718 spread) and would force a third rig.

The pads improved are CR-P1, CR-P2, CR-P4, CR-P6. The number of rigs mobilised is 2, because Kettleridge section 4 allows each mobilised rig to serve at most 2 building pads within the Phase 1 milestone window: ceil(4 pads / 2) = 2 rigs, mobilisation $80,000 (lump sum $40,000 per rig, not prorated). Rig assignments: RIG-1 serves CR-P1 and CR-P2; RIG-2 serves CR-P4 and CR-P6. One production modulus test is bought per improved pad (4 tests). Campus total cost at the project budget prices is $442,892 (footings, piers, platform, excavation, backfill, tests and mobilisation; no dewatering is needed because every bearing level, 42 in at CR-P4 and CR-P5 and 45 in elsewhere, is above the stabilised groundwater and above the 4.0 ft side-slope threshold).

Bearing elevation: the 42 in frost minimum governs at CR-P4 and CR-P5. At CR-P1, CR-P2, CR-P3 and CR-P6 the bearing level is 45 in, one 3-in step below the frost minimum, so that the 42 in thick heavy column footings keep soil cover and the stiffer allowable bearing at depth reduces footing size; deeper levels were rejected because the 1.5H:1V side slopes required below 4.0 ft more than double the excavation cost.

Governing constraint: on every pad BEARING selects the design - improved and spread footings are sized so that q_net is at or within a few percent of q_allow,net, and removing one 3-in step of width from those footings would exceed the allowable. SETTLEMENT governs individual spread footings (CR-P1 F1, CR-P3 F3, CR-P4 F1) and SLIDING the shear-wall footings of CR-P4 and CR-P5.

Structural design: thickness from two-way shear at d/2 and one-way shear at d (phi = 0.75, Vc per EM 1110-2-2104 paragraph 5.1), d = t - 4 in, minimum 12 in, rounded up to 3 in; reinforcement ratio = max(0.0018, flexural requirement at the column or wall face with phi = 0.9, 1.2D + 1.6L), provided by bars No. 5 to No. 9 at 12 in or less.

# Design basis - Phase 1 foundation strategy, Cattail Run Data Campus (AV-CR-2604)

Structural engineer of record, Phase 1 foundation package. Six pads (CR-P1 to CR-P6), each with one instrumented column line of five isolated column footings (F1-F5) and one continuous shear-wall footing (W1). Every number below is derived from the documents in the data room; the deliverables foundation_geometry.json, ground_improvement_plan.json, foundation_schedule.xlsx, foundation_feasibility_matrix.md and constraint_register.xlsx carry the same values.

## 1. Governing criteria and documents set aside

The criteria that govern are: UFC 3-220-01 Geotechnical Engineering (1 Nov 2012, Change 3, 1 Jul 2025) for bearing, factors of safety (Table 2-3), settlement limits, minimum widths and depth, frost and presumptive-value prohibition; UFC 3-301-01 Structural Engineering (2023, Change 4) for load combinations (2-4.3) and thick-footing reinforcement (1808.8.2.1); UFGS 03 30 00 paragraph 2.5.2 for the concrete exposure-class limits; the Loudoun County AHJ letter LC-BD-26-0774 (Amendment 3 frost depth, Amendment 4 no presumptive values); the Basis of Design Rev 3; the Geotechnical Data Report Rev 2 with its boring logs and laboratory summary; the civil grading and groundwater record; the load-combination memo; the RFI log; the Kettleridge proposal KGS-26-0917 for pier parameters, prices and the mobilisation rule; and the BIM parameter standard Rev 2. The analysis references applied are UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2, 2025) chapter 5 for bearing capacity and its sections 4-5.1.2/4-5.1.3 and Figure 5-41 for wall stability, EM 1110-1-1905 for the bearing-capacity cross-check and groundwater adjustment, FHWA GEC 13 chapter 5 for rammed aggregate piers and the elastic settlement equation, EM 1110-2-2502 for the sliding limit-equilibrium procedure, EM 1110-2-2104 for reinforced-concrete strength (shear per paragraph 5.1) and EM 1110-2-2000 Table 2-2 for the sulfate exposure condition.

Documents reviewed and set aside, with the reason:

- UFC 3-220-01N Foundation Design (2005) and UFC 3-220-10N Soil Mechanics (2005) were set aside because they are cancelled predecessor volumes; UFC 3-220-01 (2012, Change 3) and UFC 3-220-20 (2025) replace them.
- Geotechnical Addendum 1 was set aside because it is superseded in its entirety by Data Report Rev 2 (its Es values of 320/900/2400 ksf and its 4,000 psf presumptive value are withdrawn).
- Basis of Design Rev 1 was set aside because Rev 3 supersedes it (Rev 1 classified every building as Warehouse with F0 concrete, allowed 1-in dimensions and 20 ft depth).
- The NOAA NCEI 1951-1980 air-freezing-index tables were set aside because the AHJ letter Amendment 3 and RFI-007 name them the superseded edition of the product.
- The Broadview Commons adjacent-parcel report (5,500 psf) was set aside because it is a different property with different stratigraphy (RFI-013).
- FHWA GEC 6 (shallow foundations for bridges) was set aside because it is written for a different class of structure; its bridge movement criteria are not used.
- EM 1110-2-2104 Table 3-1 load factors were set aside because they are for hydraulic structures and the load-combination memo states they do not apply.
- The 3,000 psf presumptive value of Data Report Rev 2 section 7 and all building-code presumptive values were set aside because AHJ Amendment 4, UFC 3-220-01 2-4.5.2/2-4.6.4 and RFI-009 prohibit presumptive bearing values where a site investigation has been made.

## 2. Bearing-capacity and settlement methods applied; factor of safety at each pad

Bearing capacity was evaluated with three widely accepted methods, as UFC 3-220-01 paragraph 2-4.7.1 requires: Terzaghi (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-2/5-5), Meyerhof 1963 (Table 5-6) and Brinch Hansen 1970 (Table 5-8), each in the general drained bearing-capacity equation UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 5-15 with the drained parameters of the bearing stratum (Stratum I: phi' = 26 deg, c' = 0.25 ksf, 118 pcf); the Vesic solution of the same general equation (EM 1110-1-1905 Eq. 4-1, Table 4-4) was also computed. The groundwater correction of UFC 3-220-20 Figure 5-6 (EM 1110-1-1905 Eq. 1-6) was applied at every footing with the stabilised piezometer depths (8.0, 9.0, 19.0, 8.0, 21.0 and 8.5 ft); at CR-P1, CR-P2, CR-P4 and CR-P6 the water table lies within one footing width below the bearing level, so the N-gamma term uses the reduced average unit weight gamma_av = gamma - gamma_w (Df + B - Dw)/B. Engineering judgement under RFI-021 selects the design value: the Meyerhof (1963) solution of the general equation, which UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3 identifies as applicable to any bearing condition and suited to soils whose strength is dominated by frictional parameters (the Terzaghi method is listed for undrained conditions), capped by the Vesic solution where that is lower. The reported net allowable bearing pressure is therefore q_allow,net = min(qult,Meyerhof, qult,Vesic) / FS - sigma'zD (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 5-14, the more conservative net convention), so it is never more permissive than the general bearing-capacity equation of the foundations manual (RFI-021 test b). The Terzaghi and Brinch Hansen results are tabulated below as the lower-bound methods; the design value lies 4-19 percent above the least of the three and below the Vesic value computed with the net-ultimate convention (qult - sigma'zD)/FS. The applied net pressure is q_net = P/(B L) + (150 - 118 pcf) t under the D + L service reactions and is <= q_allow,net at every footing. No presumptive value was used anywhere.

The factor of safety at each pad is the UFC 3-220-01 Table 2-3 minimum for the STRUCTURE row assigned in Basis of Design Rev 3 section 2: FS = 3.5 at CR-P1, CR-P2, CR-P3 and CR-P6 (Light Industrial, Public); FS = 3.0 at CR-P4 (Apartments, Office); FS = 2.5 at CR-P5 (Warehouse - the Table 2-3 note calling for FS > 3 for super-flat warehouse floors is not invoked because the Basis of Design sets no such floor requirement). The same FS is used for improved footings, whose allowable pressure is conservatively the unimproved Stratum I value.

Settlement was computed by the method RFI-019 directs: layered elastic compression, s = sum(delta-sigma x H / Es), with the net stress increment from the 2 vertical to 1 horizontal distribution for a rectangular loaded area, delta-sigma = q_net B L / ((B + z)(L + z)), evaluated at the mid-height of uniform 0.25 ft layers carried to max(4B, 40 ft) below the bearing surface, with the pad-specific Es of Data Report Rev 2 and the Stratum I base interpolated by station (rounded to 0.1 ft). This is FHWA GEC 13 Eq. 5-14. For improved footings the GEC 13 two-layer method was used: upper-zone settlement s_uz = qg / kg (Eq. 5-13) with qg = q ns / (ns Ra - Ra + 1) (Eq. 5-12), plus the same layered elastic compression below the treatment depth (Eq. 5-11/5-14). Every settlement was also re-run with the layer compliance split at the stratum contacts; the larger value is reported. The subgrade-reaction estimator of the combined-footing and mat chapter (UFC 3-220-20 5-4) was not used.

## 3. Tolerable-movement criteria

The tolerable-movement criteria adopted are those of UFC 3-220-01 paragraph 2-4.7.1: total post-construction settlement not more than 1 in, and differential settlement not producing an angular distortion greater than 1/500 between adjacent foundation units (difference in settlement divided by the distance between the units). Adjacent units are F1-F2 (24 ft), F2-F3 (20 ft), F3-F4 (16 ft), F4-F5 (12 ft) and F5-W1 (5 ft, i.e. 0.12 in maximum differential). Every foundation was designed to a computed settlement of 0.97 in or less and every adjacent pair to the 1/500 limit less 0.01 in, on both layer-assignment variants. EM 1110-1-1905 paragraph 4-1b (1 in, 1/500) is consistent. The competing criterion rejected is the FHWA GEC 6 bridge criterion (angular distortion 0.004 for continuous and 0.005 for simple spans, section 5.3.1) and its 1/300 masonry figure (section 8.3.1), which are for a different class of structure and are less restrictive than the governing 1/500.

## 4. Ground-improvement design parameters and authority

- Stress concentration ratio ns = 10: FHWA GEC 13 chapter 5 section 4.2.1 value for structure foundation support under rigid footings, as directed by RFI-011 (vendor manual ratios of 20 or more are not accepted).
- Pier diameter 30 in (area 4.909 sf) and minimum clear spacing 1.0 ft (3.5 ft centres): Kettleridge proposal section 2; this fixes the maximum area replacement ratio at 0.401 (square grid) / 0.463 (staggered).
- Minimum area replacement ratio Ra = 0.33: FHWA GEC 13 section 4.2.1 (Collin 2007); adopted Ra 0.33-0.40, Ra = n x 4.909 / (B L), with the pier count checked to fit inside the footing footprint.
- Stiffness modulus kg: Kettleridge proposal section 3 as-tested pad values (CR-P1 165, CR-P2 140, CR-P4 195, CR-P6 155 pci; CR-P3 210 and CR-P5 230 pci not needed), used in GEC 13 Eq. 5-13.
- Treatment depth 8 to 25 ft below footing soffit, whole feet: Kettleridge section 2 and BoD Rev 3 section 4; adopted 8-9 ft, which carries the piers to or below the base of Stratum I at almost every improved footing.
- Maximum design top-of-pier stress 18,000 psf: Kettleridge section 2 (verified at 150 percent in the modulus test); maximum design qg = 16049 psf.
- Verification: one production modulus test per improved pad (Kettleridge section 5; GEC 13 section 4.4).
