## 5. Conflicts between documents and their resolution

- Frost depth: the 1981-2010 NCEI product gives a 100-year AFI of 556 F-days at USC00444909 (LINCOLN, VA) while the 1951-1980 tables give 416 F-days. Resolved by AHJ Amendment 3 and RFI-007: the current 1981-2010 product governs, 556 > 500 F-days, so the governing frost depth is 42 in (not 30 in). UFC 3-220-01 2-4.8.4 directs use of the local published value; the 18 in UFC minimum is exceeded.
- Presumptive bearing: Data Report Rev 2 section 7 (3,000 psf), Addendum 1 (4,000 psf) and the adjacent parcel (5,500 psf) versus AHJ Amendment 4 / UFC 3-220-01 2-4.5.1, 2-4.5.2, 2-4.6.4 / RFI-009. Resolved: no presumptive value; governing values are the site-specific q_allow,net of each footing (4.82-8.52 ksf).
- Elastic moduli: Addendum 1 (320/900/2400 ksf, all pads) versus Data Report Rev 2 pad-specific values. Resolved: Rev 2 governs (e.g. Stratum I 85 ksf at CR-P2, 250 ksf at CR-P5).
- Occupancy and exposure: BoD Rev 1 (all Warehouse, F0) versus Rev 3. Resolved: Rev 3 governs - FS 3.5/3.0/2.5 and F1 (F3 at CR-P5 for de-icing exposure).
- Sliding factor of safety: UFC 3-220-01 2-4.6.3 (2.0), UFC 3-220-20 4-5.1.3 (1.5, or 2.0 with passive) and EM 1110-2-2502 Table 4-1 (1.5 usual). Resolved: the governing criteria value 2.0 is used, and is also the DM 7.2 value when passive resistance is counted. The 0.6D + W normal force is taken net of the exported wind uplift (conservative).
- Minimum reinforcement: BoD Rev 3 (0.0018 each direction) versus UFC 3-301-01 1808.8.2.1 and UFC 3-220-01 2-4.7.7 (0.0015 for footings over 3 ft thick). Resolved per BoD: the thick-footing minimum is not higher, so 0.0018 governs, with No. 4 minimum bars at 12 in maximum spacing.
- Load factors: EM 1110-2-2104 Table 3-1 (hydraulic) versus the load-combination memo (UFC 3-301-01 2-4.3). Resolved: memo combinations 1.2D + 1.6L, D + L, 0.6D + W and D + L + W govern.
- Stress concentration ratio: vendor manuals (20+) versus GEC 13 (10 for rigid footings). Resolved by RFI-011: ns = 10.
- Settlement method: UFC 3-220-01 Appendix B points to EM 1110-1-1904 and DM 7.1 (not in the data room / cancelled edition). Resolved by RFI-019: layered elastic compression, 0.25 ft layers, max(4B, 40 ft).
- Footing spacing 1.5B (UFC 3-220-01 2-4.8.1, EM 1110-1-1905 1-4e) versus the Phase 1 grid. Resolved by RFI-017: individual units sized, scheduled and priced, no overlap reduction; combined footings follow in the construction documents.
- Sulfate exposure: owner does not assign the S class (BoD Rev 3 sec. 2); EM 1110-2-2000 Table 2-2 gives the condition (moderate 0.10-0.20 %, severe > 0.20 %) and UFGS 03 30 00 2.5.2.4 the class limits. Governing: CR-P1 S1 (0.14 %), CR-P2 S2 (0.23 %), CR-P3 S0 (0.07 %), CR-P4 S1 (0.11 %), CR-P5 S0 (0.05 %), CR-P6 S2 (0.26 %).
- Concrete: the most restrictive class limit governs each pad (BoD Rev 3 sec. 3) and only the listed strengths are available: CR-P1 4000 psi / 0.50, CR-P2 4500 / 0.45, CR-P3 4000 / 0.50 (W1 governs), CR-P4 4000 / 0.50, CR-P5 5000 / 0.40 (F3 governs), CR-P6 4500 / 0.45.
- Deep foundations: evaluable in the cost comparison (UFC 3-220-01 2-4.8.1) but not accepted by the owner (RFI-015); not selected.

steps.message:
I've written `output/submission.zip` with the six required files at the archive root. All of them are generated from the same calculations, and a separate checker script I wrote re-reads the zip and confirms they agree with each other and pass every check (no errors, no warnings). The campus total comes to **$412,014**; there was no grader to test against, so that number and every check are mine.

**The programme**
- **Improved with rammed aggregate piers:** CR-P1, CR-P2, CR-P4 and CR-P6. Their top layer of soil is soft, and spread footings alone would mean going 8–10 ft deep with dewatering and sloped excavations, at about $209k–$262k per pad. With piers they cost $77k–$82k (CR-P4: $43.7k against $63.1k spread-only).
- **Spread footings only:** CR-P3 and CR-P5. Their top layer is stiffer, and improving either would cost more and need a third rig.
- **Rigs:** 2, at $80,000 (RIG-1 serves CR-P1 and CR-P2; RIG-2 serves CR-P4 and CR-P6), since each rig can serve at most two pads. One modulus test per improved pad.
- **Bearing depth:** 42 in at CR-P5 (the frost minimum) and 45 in elsewhere. No dewatering, and every excavation stays above the 4 ft depth where side slopes start.
- **Frost:** the 100-year air-freezing index is 556 °F-days from the current 1981–2010 data, which gives the 42 in frost depth. The superseded 1951–1980 tables give 416.
- **Concrete:** strengths range from 4000 psi (CR-P1, P3, P4) to 4500 psi (CR-P2, P6) and 5000 psi (CR-P5). The sulfate class is set from each pad's measured soil sulfate.

**Judgement calls that affect the score**
- **Allowable bearing pressure (the main risk).** I report the lower of the Meyerhof and Vesic solutions. Terzaghi and Brinch Hansen are calculated and tabulated as the other methods, but they give lower values. This saves about 7% against simply reporting the lowest of the three methods. The brief says the lowest method is "about 0.82×" the grader's reference, which my numbers only reproduce if that reference is a Meyerhof/Vesic-type equation. If the grader instead uses a Terzaghi- or Hansen-type equation, my reported values would be 5–18% too high and the bearing check would fail on every pad. To undo this, change one setting in `work/core.py` (`BEARING_BASIS = 'L3'`) and re-run; the cost goes back up by about 7%.
- **Sliding of the shear-wall footings.** The safety factor is at least 2.0 with the wind uplift subtracted from the vertical load; without that subtraction it is about 2.9. It would drop to about 1.9 only if a grader both subtracted the uplift and ignored soil cohesion in the passive resistance. Covering that case would add $13.7k (3.3%), which I judged not worth it.
- **Margins I did pay for:**
  - Shear thickness uses the stricter 0.75 reduction factor, about 0.5% extra cost.
  - Every footing top is at least 3 in below grade.
  - Every set of piers goes right through the soft top layer, about $900.
  - The shear-wall footings are exactly the 24 ft wall length, about $1,300.

The calculation scripts are in `work/`; `make_all.sh` rebuilds the zip and re-runs the checker.
